one_line: Shadowy late Ganga ruler of Jajnagar facing Firuz Shah Tughlaq’s invasions in the 1350s.

appearance.face: oval face, medium brown Odia complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes with a thoughtful, slightly worried default expression, neatly trimmed short moustache and light stubble along the jaw
appearance.hair: straight black hair to the nape of the neck, smoothed back under a simple gold cloth turban (paga) with a narrow red band at the base and a small central green gemstone bezel
appearance.costume: a knee-length cream cotton tunic (angarkha-style) with side-tie folds and faint woven stripes, over a deep red silk dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated in front, bordered with a thin gold trim; a dark green cotton shawl draped from left shoulder across the torso and around the back, simple gold armbands on both upper arms, a short strand of small gold beads at the neck, and plain leather sandals, all styled in 14th‑century coastal Odisha court fashion.
appearance.signature: a ceremonial Odia straight sword with a gently flared tip, iron blade, and a simple gold hilt wrapped in dark red cloth, carried sheathed at his left hip with the scabbard in dark brown leather and minimal brass fittings

ref_desc: Bhanu Deva III has an oval medium-brown face, short black hair under a gold turban, cream tunic, deep red dhoti, dark green shawl, simple gold ornaments, brown sandals, and a dark red-hilt Odia sword in a brown scabbard, with a thoughtful worried expression.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Bhanu Deva III: an early-30s, lean Odia king with an oval medium-brown face, sharp dark eyes, straight nose, and a thoughtful slightly worried expression, sporting a short moustache and light jaw stubble. His straight black hair is smoothed back and mostly hidden under a simple gold cloth turban with a narrow red band and a small central green gemstone. He wears a knee-length cream cotton angarkha-style tunic with side ties and faint woven stripes over a tightly wrapped deep red silk dhoti with a thin gold border, plus a dark green shawl draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back. Add plain gold armbands on both upper arms, a short strand of small gold beads at the neck, and simple brown leather sandals to match 14th-century coastal Odisha court attire. At his left hip, show his signature ceremonial Odia straight sword with a gently flared tip, an iron blade, and a gold hilt wrapped in dark red cloth, sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings. Use a palette dominated by cream, deep red, dark green, gold, and brown, and pose him upright in a neutral stance that shows his costume and weapon clearly.
